The first computer language I learned was Fortran, way back in 1975. I learned on a system that used Hollerith cards, you know - IBM punch cards. You had to laboriously type (and punch) each line of your program on an individual card you'd loaded into a teletype console. Then you took your card deck and loaded it into a card reader that was about the size of a Volkswagen Beetle. On a Control Data Corporation computer that used magnetic cores for memory. Learning Fortran was a fascinating thing, being so different from anything else I'd ever done, except possibly for algebra. I went on to learn Basic, Cobol, System/370 Assembly Language, PL/1, GPSSV, IBM PC Assembly Language and Pascal. Fortran was clunky and awkward in many ways, but it was a wonderful feeling, being able to make this giant machine (the CDC mainframe took up a whole huge room) jump through hoops. Tape drives spun, lights flashed, the card reader shook the floor, it was fabulous. :)
I still use Fortran regularly (most days), albeit using a modern Intel Fortran compiler, it has come a loooong way :)
Fortran was wonderful compared to Basic. Pascal was better still and C beat them all. Since then not so much.
